title: Appendix: A Tale of Two Worlds
author: Gordon Calleja
phase2_revision_note: User verification 2026-05-11: methodology lives in IG-03, NOT in this appendix. This unit is PROFILE-ONLY (WoW + Planetside + binary-comparative scaffold). The Phase 1 plan-vs-finding correction (no methodology section in the appendix) is preserved and amplified.

outline.function: Disclaims pedagogical purpose: appendix is for readers unfamiliar with MMOGs; explicitly NOT a methodology statement; identifies WoW and Planetside as the two worlds inhabited by research participants.

Defines MMORPG vs MMOFPS; locates WoW within MMORPG lineage descending from pen-and-paper RPGs (D&D 1974); flags that the role-playing tag is misleading because most MMORPG players do not perform-in-character; defines MMOFPS by twitch-based long-range combat and first-person perspective; notes support classes; concludes that the boundary is porous (a product of setting and weapon availability).

Spatial design contrast. Azeroth: 96 regions, 2 continents, Alliance/Horde factions + contested areas, aesthetic-palette differentiation, abrupt non-mimetic transitions, designed channels (mountains/forests/walls/shores) creating impassable boundaries. Auraxis: 10 continents + 5 caverns, visually generic, weather-cycled, no AI agents in empty areas, no urban centers, no marketplaces/auction houses/taverns, equipment-terminal economy, pervasive PvP precluding casual socializing.

Narrative scaffolding contrast. WoW: Warcraft RTS trilogy backstory, shallow vs Tolkien/Greenwood; Haelvon and Nombril quotations evidence functional disinterest in quest text; lore is not required for progression. Planetside: futuristic three-faction premise (Terran Empire, New Conglomerate, Vanu Sovereignty) on Auraxis.

Server architecture contrast. WoW: thousands of clone servers, region-locked (Americas/Australasia/Europe/Asia) creating mobility-friction across geographies. Ananke quotation documents social continuity across SWG/WoW/DDO maintained across continental relocations. Planetside: three clone servers (US West, US East, Europe), no regional restrictions.

Identity axis contrast. WoW: race/class selection, restricted avatar customization (hair/skin/face), Inauro quotation evidences participant dissatisfaction, differentiation collapses into gear ('you literally are what you wear'). Planetside: less avatar customization still, but no character classes; identity emerges from skill-and-certification combinations as play progresses.

Action-system contrast in depth. Latency: WoW tolerates 300ms (queued moves), Planetside latency-sensitive (real-time aim). Perspective: WoW 3rd-person unanimously preferred for wider FOV, Planetside 1st-person mandatory for aiming. Environmental effects: rain/light materially affect Planetside combat (infiltrator suits, occluded sight, cover/elevation), trivial in WoW. Level structure: WoW level-gated absolute power, mobs/PvP scaled by level-difference, griefing/corpse-camping. Planetside levels confer certifications not absolute power, enabling new-character competitiveness via tactics. Specialization: WoW classes (rogue) lack required-role quests; Planetside support roles (engineer/medic/hacker/driver) are tactically irreplaceable and rewarded via shared XP. Baal quotation: tactical role specialization.

Synthesizes the agency-and-emergence axis. WoW = tightly scripted, restrictive, solo-friendly, low world-mutability (respawning mobs/NPCs/resources); Planetside = open-ended, player-event-generative, mass-collaborative, persistent territorial conquest (continent capture has lasting strategic value). Kumacho quotation: outfit organization (D2A, GoTR) can change battle shape. Closing claim: both games are prototypes of their respective genres and have served as sites for developing a new model for player involvement; future application will update the model.

concepts.label: MMO-genre-profile
concepts.definition: A pedagogical-cum-analytic genre description that triangulates a game through genre lineage, topography, lore, server architecture, customization economy, and action mechanics.

concepts.label: MMORPG-vs-MMOFPS distinction
concepts.definition: A porous genre boundary distinguished principally by combat system (queued/turn-tolerant vs twitch/real-time), perspective default (3rd vs 1st person), and setting (weapon density).

concepts.label: virtual-topography
concepts.definition: The aesthetic-and-functional spatial design of a persistent world, where designed channels, impassable boundaries, palette differentiation, and density of social spaces (or their absence) condition modes of inhabitation.

concepts.label: lore-as-narrative-scaffold
concepts.definition: Story-and-world-backstory whose functional weight is decoupled from gameplay progression; tolerated rather than inhabited by most MMOG players.

concepts.label: clone-worlds (parallel servers)
concepts.definition: The shard/server architecture by which a single virtual world exists as many region-divided or non-region-divided instances, each developing distinct social-economic histories.

concepts.label: customization-as-identity-axis
concepts.definition: The avatar-and-skill differentiation economy through which players individuate; in WoW collapses into gear ('you are what you wear'), in Planetside into certification combinations.

concepts.label: latency-tolerant-vs-latency-sensitive-mechanics
concepts.definition: Action-systems differ in their sensitivity to network delay; queued-action MMORPGs tolerate 300ms+, real-time-aim MMOFPSs do not.

concepts.label: perspective-affordance
concepts.definition: 3rd-person view affords wider environmental awareness at the cost of aiming precision; 1st-person view affords aim at the cost of peripheral awareness.

concepts.label: level-gated-absolute-power vs certification-specialization
concepts.definition: WoW levels confer absolute power differentials that determine social mobility and PvP viability; Planetside levels expand the certification menu without conferring inherent superiority.

concepts.label: griefing-and-corpse-camping
concepts.definition: Asymmetric-power abuse-patterns in level-gated PvP worlds where higher-level characters repeatedly kill lower-level victims at resurrection points; socially frowned upon but rule-permitted.

concepts.label: support-role-economy-and-shared-XP
concepts.definition: Reward-system design where non-combatant roles (medic, engineer, hacker, driver) accumulate XP from teammates' actions, structurally incentivizing collaboration.

concepts.label: emergent-vs-scripted-gameplay
concepts.definition: Spectrum from designer-pre-scripted events (WoW quests, instanced battlegrounds, respawning mobs) to player-generated tactical situations (Planetside continental campaigns).

concepts.label: world-mutability-and-agency
concepts.definition: The degree to which player action persistently alters the game world; near-zero in WoW (respawning resources/mobs/NPCs), substantive in Planetside (continent control persists).

concepts.label: binary-comparative-scaffold
concepts.definition: Calleja's analytic apparatus that organizes case-presentation along symmetric axes (genre, topography, lore, server, customization, mechanics, agency) to triangulate a model across two contrasting prototypes.

concepts.label: prototypicality-as-case-selection-criterion
concepts.definition: Calleja's closing justification for case selection: each game prototypes its genre, encompassing gameplay forms shared with other genres while exhibiting the massively-multiplayer element.

concepts.label: participant-quotation-embedding
concepts.definition: An evidentiary move in which scholarly claims about game features are anchored by short participant interview quotations (Haelvon, Nombril, Ananke, Inauro, Baal, Kumacho).

positions.label: WoW-as-prototypical-MMORPG
positions.claim: World of Warcraft, despite criticisms of its lore depth and customization economy, instantiates the genre prototype: pen-and-paper RPG lineage, level-gated absolute power, queued latency-tolerant action, gear-as-identity, scripted quest economy.
positions.supporting_evidence: pp. 187-200, all subsections; closing synthesis p. 200.

positions.label: Planetside-as-prototypical-MMOFPS
positions.claim: Planetside instantiates the MMOFPS prototype: real-time twitch combat, mandatory first-person perspective, certification-specialization, environmentally-sensitive tactics, persistent territorial conquest, emergent mass collaboration.
positions.supporting_evidence: pp. 187-200, all subsections; closing synthesis p. 200.

positions.label: the-binary-comparative-scaffold-is-the-method
positions.claim: The appendix's structural device (symmetric WoW-then-Planetside subsections along seven axes) is itself a methodological apparatus: it triangulates the player-involvement model across two genre prototypes, demonstrating its cross-genre applicability.
positions.supporting_evidence: Eight subsections each constructed as WoW-then-Planetside; closing claim about prototypicality justifying both case selection and generalization.

tensions.label: cohabitation-vs-competition
poles: WoW emphasizes cohabitation: marketplaces, auction houses, taverns, persistent player-economies, social channels
Planetside emphasizes competition: factional warfare, equipment terminals, no social spaces, pervasive PvP
tensions.function: Generates the most consequential design-divergence: social-space density correlates with economy-structure and with the kind of player-involvement each world cultivates.

tensions.label: persistent-progression-vs-cyclical-warfare
poles: WoW's level-and-gear progression accretes individually across time but the world resets (mobs/NPCs/resources respawn)
Planetside's character progression is flat-after-certifications but the world persistently records territorial conquest
tensions.function: Inverts the locus of persistence: WoW persists characters and resets worlds, Planetside resets characters (relatively flat power) and persists worlds (continent control accrues).

tensions.label: scripted-content-vs-emergent-content
poles: WoW's quest and instanced-battleground economy delivers pre-designed gameplay
Planetside provides only mechanics and uninhabited terrain, requiring players to generate events
tensions.function: Operationalizes the agency axis: where does the gameplay content come from, designer or player community?

interlocutors.name: Fine, G.A.
interlocutors.role: pen-and-paper RPG performance — only theorist cited in appendix body

wow_profile_capture.genre: MMORPG; descends from pen-and-paper RPGs (D&D 1974); role-playing tag is misleading since most players don't perform-in-character outside role-playing servers (pp. 187-188).
wow_profile_capture.topography: Azeroth, 96 regions, 2 continents, Alliance/Horde + contested areas; non-mimetic aesthetic-palette differentiation; designed channels (mountains/forests/walls/shores) creating impassable boundaries; abrupt regional transitions accepted by participants; quiltlike terrain (p. 188-189).
wow_profile_capture.social_spaces: Marketplaces, auction houses, taverns; player-driven economy with trade-channel advertising and geographic proximity for transactions (p. 190).
wow_profile_capture.lore: Warcraft RTS trilogy backstory; shallow vs Tolkien/Greenwood; functional disinterest among participants (Haelvon, Nombril); progress decoupled from lore (pp. 190-192).
wow_profile_capture.server_architecture: Thousands of clone servers, region-locked (Americas/Australasia/Europe/Asia); cross-region play impossible; relocation breaks friend-groups unless they migrate (pp. 192-193).
wow_profile_capture.customization: Race/class selection at creation; limited avatar customization (hair/skin/face); differentiation through gear; 'you literally are what you wear'; Inauro: dagger vs sword rogue builds (p. 193).
wow_profile_capture.mechanics: 300ms latency-tolerant via queued actions; tab-targeting; 3rd-person preferred for wider FOV; environment minimally affects combat (only distance + passable/impassable) (pp. 194-196).
wow_profile_capture.progression: Level-gated absolute power; XP from quests, kills, battlegrounds; mob aggro radius scales with level-difference; help-site usage normalized (pp. 195-196).
wow_profile_capture.questing: Deliver-X / kill-X / find-Y structure; quest text often unread; functional play rewards efficiency over creativity (p. 196).
wow_profile_capture.pvp_and_griefing: PvP servers permit corpse-camping and griefing of lower-level victims; rule-permitted, socially frowned upon (pp. 196-197).
wow_profile_capture.specialization: Rogue class detects traps / opens locks but no quests require this specifically; classes are not tactically irreplaceable (p. 198).
wow_profile_capture.world_mutability: Near-zero: mobs/NPCs/resources respawn; outpost capture has no lasting reward (pp. 199-200).
wow_profile_capture.agency: Solo-friendly (quests, crafting, auction-house economics); limited scope for world-altering action (pp. 199-200).

planetside_profile_capture.genre: MMOFPS; distinguished by long-range twitch-based combat; first-person dominant; accommodates non-fighting support classes (medics, engineers, transport drivers); porous boundary with MMORPGs (pp. 187-188).
planetside_profile_capture.topography: Auraxis, 10 continents + 5 caverns; weather-cycled but visually generic; participants struggle to differentiate continents; no AI agents in empty areas (barrenness); no urban areas; Sanctuary is the only safe zone (pp. 189-190).
planetside_profile_capture.social_spaces: Absent. No marketplaces, auction houses, taverns; equipment-terminal economy; socializing restricted to outfit chat; fast-paced PvP precludes casual gathering (p. 190).
planetside_profile_capture.lore: Futuristic space-colonization-gone-wrong; three factions (Terran Empire, New Conglomerate, Vanu Sovereignty); allegiance-pledge required (pp. 191-192).
planetside_profile_capture.server_architecture: Three clone servers (US West, US East, Europe); no regional restrictions (pp. 192-193).
planetside_profile_capture.customization: Minimal avatar (face/hair/head); no classes; identity emerges from skill-and-certification combinations during play; Inauro analogue absent — no participant complaint surfaced on avatar appearance (pp. 193-194).
planetside_profile_capture.mechanics: Real-time latency-sensitive aim; mandatory first-person; environment materially affects combat (rain occludes line of sight, light affects detection, cover/elevation crucial) (pp. 194-196).
planetside_profile_capture.progression: Level confers certification points, not absolute power; starting character can defeat advanced character via tactics/timing/numbers; specialization expands rather than gates (pp. 197-198).
planetside_profile_capture.questing: No designer-scripted missions; events are player-generated; situations unpredictable, often unbalanced (5:1 sieges) but pleasurable as desperate-defense scenarios (pp. 198-199).
planetside_profile_capture.pvp_and_griefing: PvP is the world's medium not a sub-mode; no griefing/corpse-camping motif because power asymmetries don't accumulate (pp. 197-198).
planetside_profile_capture.specialization: Hackers irreplaceable for facility-sabotage; medics revive; engineers repair; drivers operate mass-transport vehicles; shared XP rewards collaboration even outside one's squad/platoon (p. 198).
planetside_profile_capture.world_mutability: Substantive: continent capture persists; spawn-point control accumulates; connected facilities give faction-wide benefits (pp. 199-200).
planetside_profile_capture.agency: Strong sense of agency through tactical concerted effort; outfits (D2A, GoTR) can change battle outcomes; mass collaboration is the structural attractor (pp. 198-200).
dimension_relevance: narrative-involvement (weak: lore decoupled, but factional allegiance anchors)
spatial-involvement (medium: weather and cover matter, but aesthetic generic)
affective-involvement (strong: emergent desperate-defense scenarios; outfit devotion)

case_study_template_extraction.abstract_scaffold: For each game studied: (1) Genre placement and lineage; (2) Topography (regions, transitions, social-space density); (3) Lore (depth, player engagement, progression-decoupling); (4) Server architecture (sharding, regional restrictions, social-continuity effects); (5) Customization (avatar + skill axes, identity economy); (6) Mechanics (latency, perspective, environmental effects, level structure, specialization); (7) Agency and world-mutability (scripted vs emergent, persistence of player action).
case_study_template_extraction.evidentiary_pattern: Each axis-claim is anchored by short participant quotations interleaved with analytic narration (Haelvon, Nombril, Ananke, Inauro, Baal, Kumacho).
case_study_template_extraction.case-selection_logic: Each case prototypes its genre; together they encompass gameplay forms shared with other genres while exhibiting the massively-multiplayer element; future application updates the model.
case_study_template_extraction.dissertation_portability: Directly transferable as a case-presentation template for the dissertation's empirical-adaptation chapter (combined with IG-03 methodology). The dissertation can adapt the seven-axis scaffold to its corpus of cases; the participant-quotation embedding pattern is methodologically portable; the prototypicality justification supplies a defensible case-selection criterion.
case_study_template_extraction.calleja_self-positioning: The closing paragraph (p. 200) frames the appendix as having supplied 'solid foundational research' for developing 'a new model for player involvement' (the player-involvement model, PIM) and anticipates 'future application of the model to other genres' — explicitly invitational toward successor case studies, which is the rhetorical opening the dissertation occupies.

production_editorial_anomaly.finding: Figures labeled 'Figure 12.1' (p. 189) and 'Figure 12.2' (p. 191) inside a section presented as 'Appendix' in TOC and running heads.
production_editorial_anomaly.interpretation: MIT Press production likely treated the appendix as an internal Chapter 12 during typesetting, leaving the figure-numbering artifact when the appendix designation was finalized. Suggests the appendix was conceived/drafted as a chapter and demoted in editorial pass.
production_editorial_anomaly.substantive_implication: Reinforces the claim that the appendix is functionally more than pedagogical — it carries chapter-weight case-study material that the structural designation 'appendix' under-represents.

cross_pipeline_bridges.primary: Combined with IG-03 methodology (Ch.3 pp. 35-36), this appendix supplies the case-study template for the dissertation's empirical-adaptation chapter.
secondary: Spatial-design dissertation chapter: Topographies subsection (designed channels, aesthetic vs mimetic terrain).
Emergent-vs-scripted gameplay dissertation chapter: Closing Planetside synthesis (player-generated events, persistent territorial conquest).
